I hsve one friend on Blue most of the time, what that means is if they're in Invite+, VRChat wont tell me where they are, but when I do an invite request to them, I get an invite without their action. 

I wonder if VRChat has changed some of the other aspects of Invite+?

details:
Preface:  I just hosted an Invite+ instance, and it's been a WHILE since I tried bringing a few friends to one in order to hang out.  I was then told that my friend could not invite someone to the world.  Why not?  I feel like I've been completely misled as this means Invite+ works in a completely different way than Friends+ and Group+ in their own respective arenas.  Again, I iterate on the idea of it being misleading.

So, I was told this isn't a bug?  I swear, I SWEAR Invite+ instances used to mean that users who were inside as well as the host could invite people, and I ALSO SWEAR, way back users who were on Green status in a Friends+ still had to be requested on to join.  I've not been inside of an Invite instance in a long time, and so I apparently was not aware that Invite+ instances didn't work that way.

What?

Okay, so hear me out.  What's the point then of an Invite+ instance?  Or, to double down, what's the point in there being a Join Me (Blue) status when Online (Green) works no differently?  Friends+ Instances can just be joined on if you're on Green status, so what's the point of Blue?  I thought that was a bug that users were able to join without requesting.  I thought that Blue status meant people could join freely, Green meant people could see what you were doing and then request, Orange meant people couldn't see, and could request, and then Red meant people couldn't see, and couldn't request.

I SWEAR it worked like that once upon a time.  Why doesn't it?

Logically speaking, in my eyes, the instance types have less bearing then they should.  If other people in my Invite+ can't invite, like in Friends+ users can also bring friends, then..

What am I missing here?  I feel like Invite+ doesn't even need to exist if they can't.

To further clarify, is an Invite+ not more "private" than a Friends+ instance, in the sense that the host of the instance is more controlling?  That invites are passed to the host to accept and deny?

I just don't understand VRChat's social system in it's current configuration.  It doesn't feel usable in the senses that I thought it should be.  Public, Friends, and Invite instances are the only ones that make sense in my eyes, if everything in the current model is intentional, with the four status indicators available.

My request is to make instance types make more logical sense.  Invite+ should also allow other users to invite.  Just as well, Green status should not allow users to automatically join the instance, simply see what world I'm inside of so that I can let people know what I'm doing, but not implicitly allow them inside.

One could argue that they can just go through all the worlds anyway.  Sure, but they could do that if you're on Orange status, or Red status for that matter.  If you're a creature of habit, you're bound to be in one of your standard holdouts.

Of course, bonus suggestion, just make an Offline mode so that people don't know I'm online.  Would work great with Offline requests existing now frankly!
title: Instance Types make no logical sense
